text: 52. DEATH VALLEY Two hours in 120-degree heat and this daytime nightmare has turned into what Alek had predicted: A death march across Death Valley. Jimmy can’t tell if he’s been walking for two hours or a day. Time doesn’t work right out here. It’s just sun, glare, breath, footfall. His mouth feels like sandpaper. His tongue feels too big for his teeth. Every swallow is dry. His strap screen shows what he already knows: heart rate high, temperature climbing. No coordinates. No cache. No mercy. Two options scream inside his head: Find water. Get help. But maybe the only way to get help at this point is for one of them to push the red button.
